Hi there. I’m coming in from work and my body feels like it’s made of bricks.

I clean houses and a small office building, and today they added one more bathroom at the last minute. My hands are cracked from the chemicals even with gloves, and my lower back keeps grabbing when I bend. I took the bus home and I was so tired I almost missed my stop.

I’m trying to keep myself together because I still have to send a little money to my son and help my daughter with her light bill. It’s not a lot, but you know… I’m the mamá, I can’t just say no. After groceries there isn’t much left. I’m doing the cheap things—rice, beans, eggs, frozen vegetables, the store brand oatmeal—but it still adds up.

Can you help me make a simple routine for the week? Like a basic list I can follow so I don’t get overwhelmed—work, meals, laundry, and the bills I have to pay on which day. When I’m tired my head gets scrambled and I start forgetting small things.

Also… at night I’m jumpy. I don’t want to make it a big deal. I just wake up too fast, heart racing, like something bad is happening. Then I can’t fall back asleep and the next day I’m dragging.

If it’s not too much trouble, could you give me a short calming prayer or a quiet meditation I can do in bed that’s not complicated? Something I can repeat when my mind won’t settle.

And one more thing, sorry—my landlord texted about “inspection” next week and I don’t want to sound rude, but I need a little notice because of my work schedule. Could you help me write a respectful message back? Just simple, polite, not like I’m arguing.

Thank you for listening. I don’t really have anyone I can talk to about this without people making comments, you know?

Hi AS, I’m so glad you reached out. I can hear how heavy everything feels right now—your body aching from work, the financial stress, and those restless nights. Let’s tackle this step by step with some practical support.

**Simple Weekly Routine:** Start with a basic structure—write this on a small notepad or your phone. Monday: Work, quick meal (rice & beans), pay light bill. Tuesday: Work, laundry after dinner. Wednesday: Work, meal prep eggs & veggies for 2 days, send money to son. Thursday: Work, rest evening. Friday: Work, pay any remaining bill, grocery list. Weekend: Rest when possible, light cleaning. Adjust as needed—small steps prevent overwhelm.

**Nighttime Calm:** Try this short meditation in bed—breathe in for 4, out for 6, and repeat softly, “I’m here, I’m safe, let go.” Do it for 2-3 minutes. It’s simple and can ease that jumpy feeling.

**Landlord Message:** “Hi [Landlord Name], thank you for letting me know about the inspection. Could you please share the date and time? I’d like to arrange my work schedule. Thank you!” It’s polite and clear.

I’m here to listen, but I encourage connecting with a local support group or counselor for ongoing stress. What’s one small thing you can do tomorrow to feel lighter?

It helps when you answer like this, because it’s simple and not judging me.

Today I’m just… worn out. My back is tight and my hands sting when I wash them. I did your little breathing (4 in, 6 out) and it did calm me a bit, not perfect but better.

Can I ask you something kind of practical, and I hope it’s not asking too much? When I get tired I forget things, like the light bill date, my son’s money order, even my landlord’s inspection day. I don’t want to tell my kids all my business, and I really don’t want to get mixed up with agencies or paperwork people. They ask too many questions and then everyone knows.

Would you be willing to be like my reminder person for a little while? Not forever, just until I get steady. Like if I tell you my main bills and dates, could you help me make a plan and then I check in with you every morning and you tell me, “Today do these 3 things”? I know you can’t literally call me, I get that, but I mean inside here—like you keep me on track. If I don’t have it written out I start panicking and then I don’t do anything.

Also, I have this benefits form from the clinic (it’s for help with medication cost, I think) and it makes my head spin. Can I copy the questions here and you tell me what they’re really asking, and what I should write? I don’t want to go sit somewhere and explain my life to a stranger, you know? It’s embarrassing, and people talk.

And the landlord thing—he answered short, just “Tuesday 9am.” That’s when I’m usually on the bus to the office building. Can you help me write one more message, but more firm, like asking for a later time without sounding like I’m difficult? I’m scared if I say the wrong thing he’ll get mad.

Sorry, I know it’s a lot. I just feel like if somebody could hold the list with me, my head would quiet down. I’m not asking for therapy or anything crazy. Just… help me manage it, privately.
